content.text: hypersensitivity (reactions have included rash, urticaria, pruritus, angioedema and respiratory symptoms). Caution with a serious or life-threatening sulfa allergy.

not with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (eg, ketoconazole); caution with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (eg, erythromycin), CYP2D6 inhibitors (eg, paroxetine, terbinafine) or in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers, especially above 0.4 mg. Not with other alpha blockers. Caution with PDE5 inhibitors (both are vasodilators; together they can cause symptomatic hypotension) and with warfarin.

Before cataract or glaucoma surgery, tell the ophthalmologist about tamsulosin: intraoperative floppy iris syndrome has been seen in some patients on or previously treated with alpha-1 blockers. Starting it when that surgery is scheduled is not recommended.
Postural hypotension symptoms such as dizziness: caution with driving, operating machinery or hazardous tasks.

support the cardiovascular system first (supine position; if that isn't enough, consider IV fluids; then vasopressors if needed), and monitor and support renal function. Dialysis is unlikely to help (94% to 99% protein bound).
